To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the sensitivity of V/Q scan for acute PE is 86%, the specificity is 94%, and the negative predictive value is 99%.
fast CT and MR angiography are both accurate and reliable in the diagnosis of PE, and that they may have a role in the management of patients with PE in the near future.

the V/Q scan is the most frequently used screening tool for PE; that pulmonary angiography remains the reference standard for the definitive diagnosis of acute PE; that the role of fast CT and MRI in the evaluation of PE has yet to be defined; and that the role of intraarterial DDA has yet to be determined.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new methods for the diagnosis and treatment of cancer.
the development of a new class of patients.
the development of novel methods of image reconstruction and analysis for medical imaging applications.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
fast CT and MR techniques are promising, but not yet ready for widespread use as screening tools for acute pulmonary emboli.
the V/Q scan, fast CT, and MR imaging are all useful noninvasive screening modalities for the diagnosis of clinically significant PE.
a V/Q scan is the most practical, cost-effective and widely available method for screening the majority of patients for PE.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
fast CT and MR angiography have a role in the diagnosis of acute pulmonary emboli, but they are still in their infancy and require further clinical experience and outcome analysis.
fast CT and MR techniques are promising noninvasive screening tools for PE that should be further evaluated.
fast CT and MR angiography techniques are not ready for routine use in the diagnosis of PE in patients without a high pretest probability of the disease.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we should not be using the term pulmonary emboli to refer to a finding on imaging studies that are less than the size of a 4-5 mm clot.
fast CT, MR, and DSA techniques can be used in combination with V/Q scans in the management of PE.
we should not rely on a V/Q alone to make the diagnosis of PE in patients who have a high probability of PE on clinical grounds.
